messages:
sara-sales: FYI AcmeFin POC failing when we switch to their VPC private endpoint. App gets TLS handshake errors + frequent timeouts. Can we swarm?
ben-se: Thanks — can you paste the error logs from the client? Also which endpoint exactly (hostname/IP)?
sara-sales: Root message: Connecting to api.private.acmefin.internal:443 -> openssl error: 'SSL routines:tls_construct_client_hello:no protocols available' then curl -v shows 'SSL: connection reset by peer' and lots of 504s in our LB logs.
alex-sre: Hmm. That openssl error usually means TLS negotiation aborted. Could be SNI mismatch or middlebox (proxy/firewall) dropping. Do we resolve the host to a private IP?
ben-se: I ran dig from their jump host earlier: 
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> api.private.acmefin.internal
;; ANSWER SECTION:
api.private.acmefin.internal. 300 IN A 10.12.5.33
```
So DNS resolves to a RFC1918 IP in the VPC.
chris-eng: Are we terminating TLS at our private endpoint or passing through to Redwood control plane? The POC uses Private API endpoint that expects a TLS connection to our service inside their VPC via a VPC endpoint (IP).
maria-net: Two quick checks: security group rules on the ENI for the endpoint (ingress from their app SG on 443), route table to NAT/IGW, and any outbound stateful firewall that might be doing TLS inspection. Also confirm there isn't an intercepting proxy requiring client cert.
ben-se: I asked their infra to run `openssl s_client -connect 10.12.5.33:443 -servername api.private.acmefin.internal -showcerts -state -debug` — their output: 
```
CONNECTED(00000005)
139841...:error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number:../ssl/record/ssl3_record.c:332:
---
No peer certificate available
```
alex-sre: "wrong version number" often means the remote side is speaking plaintext or there's an HTTP proxy in-between. Could also be a TLS version/Cipher mismatch but less likely. Any TLS terminator?
sara-sales: Acme infra says they have a firewall that does TLS inspection (proxy) for egress and their security team enabled a TLS intercept on the subnet we are targeting. They assumed we would accept the proxy cert.
chris-eng: That explains "No peer certificate" and reset. Our endpoint expects client TLS to our certificate chain (we're not configured for MITM). We can support a proxy but they need to forward SNI and not re-sign without adding our CA to trust store. Two options: 1) Disable interception for the specific endpoint (recommended). 2) Configure mutual TLS with a client cert they provide so their proxy can forward the connection raw.
maria-net: Also noticed their route table for the subnet doesn't have a NAT gateway; egress to internet may be blocked, so OCSP/CRL checks from our side could fail if they try to validate certs externally. If they have strict egress, they might be breaking validation.
ben-se: Another data point: tcpdump on their app host shows the SYN, SYN-ACK, then immediate RST after TLS ClientHello. That pattern fits a proxy resetting when it can't handle the cert chain or SNI mapping.
sara-sales: Security asked for an allowlist of IPs to open in their perimeter. What's the minimal set we need for POC (control plane + model traffic)?
chris-eng: For Private POC we need the customer to allow outbound to: our control-plane IPs and regional model-serving IPs. For the POC we can provide a fixed set of egress IPs: 34.201.12.10, 34.201.12.11, 34.201.12.12 (note: POC-only NATed IPs). They also need to allow outbound DNS (53 UDP/TCP) to their resolver and not hijack internal resolution.
maria-net: If they're using split-horizon/private hosted zones, ensure the A record points to the endpoint ENI and not the public endpoint. Also confirm their resolver returns consistent answers from all AZs.
alex-sre: Actionable triage steps we agreed on:
- Acme infra to disable TLS interception for api.private.acmefin.internal (or add our CA to the proxy trust store) — owner: Acme security (assigned).
- Acme infra to open egress to our POC IP allowlist on 443 and allow OCSP/CRL egress if their proxy terminates TLS — owner: Acme network.
- Acme infra to confirm the endpoint SG allows inbound from the app SG on 443 and route table has no blackhole/NAT problem — owner: Acme net.
- We (chris-eng) will enable a debug endpoint that returns a simple 200 on 443 without cert validation to test plain TCP reachability — ETA 2h.
- ben-se will collect packet captures and logs and post them in this thread.

Can we get owners + ETA from Acme in this thread?

deploy-bot: New POC task created: #POC-4321 — Endpoint triage, assigned to chris-eng and ben-se, due 2026-04-02.

sara-sales: Thanks team — Acme said they'll try disabling interception and open the allowlist. They'll update by EOD PST. If that doesn't work we escalate to eng-networking for an environment walkthrough.

ben-se: If they can't disable the proxy quickly, alternative quick test: have them deploy a temporary jump-host in same subnet and run `curl --resolve "api.private.acmefin.internal:443:10.12.5.33" -v https://api.private.acmefin.internal/health` and post the raw curl output. That isolates DNS from TLS issues.

chris-eng: I'll stand by and will also prepare a fallback plan: create a temporary customer-specific endpoint that accepts connections on a non-TLS port so they can validate routing first.

maria-net: Noted for future: add checklist to POC runbook for Private endpoints (DNS split-horizon, NGW/NAT, SGs, TLS interception, OCSP egress, IP allowlist). Will draft and share.

sara-sales: Great — keeping this thread as source of truth. Thanks everyone.

ben-se: pinging eng-networking in case they want to shadow: @chris-eng @maria-net will loop in eng-networking once Acme confirms.

alex-sre: Marking as triage in customer tracker. If Acme confirms disabling interception but still fails, we should capture `openssl s_client -connect` + `tcpdump` and open an incident to correlate with our LB traces.

sara-sales: Update 3h later from Acme: they disabled TLS inspection and opened the allowlist. The curl health check now returns 200. They said tests look good. Will confirm POC flows tomorrow. :tada:
